thread:
alice: deploy-bot blocked the payments-service rollout in eu-west-1, reason: db-compat-check WARNING

deploy-bot: [automated] preflight: db-compat-check returned non-fatal warnings for payments-service: 'nullable default change on charge_ref' See /infra/sql-checks#db-compat

ben: got it — what does the warning actually mean for runtime?

carol: it flags schema diffs that could cause older workers to fail if they assume a non-null default. usually safe if we deploy consumers after writers, but we have some back-pressure consumers in prod. :thinking_face:

alice: timeline: canary already at 10% in eu-west-1, errors spiked from 0 -> ~0.5% request failures after canary started. stacktrace points to payments-worker when reading charge_ref. attaching logs snippet:
```
Error: null value in column "charge_ref" violates not-null constraint
  at payments/worker/processCharge (/app/worker.js:213:45)
  at async handler (/app/worker.js:45:5)
```

paul: options: 1) roll back the canary (fast) 2) manual rollforward + hotfix feature flag to guard reader (slower, keeps canary progress) 3) pin chart to previous values and retry after cutoff window. change window is open for another 40m.

ben: prefer rollforward if we can ship a quick guard — we have a small patch that checks charge_ref and NOPs on nulls. low-risk.

carol: agree. if we rollforward, we must update release notes and annotate the deployment with migration-safe=true and note the guard flag. also ensure Dedicated traffic shaping doesn't send heavy reads during migration.

alice: testing patch in staging now. if green, we'll manual rollforward and deploy flag: `--set feature.toggle.null-safe-charge=true`

deploy-bot: [automated] paused canary progression due to preflight warnings. manual approval required to continue. run `/deploy approve payments-service eu-west-1 --reason "null-safe guard enabled"` to proceed.

ben: staging unit tests passed, smoke ok on staging. patch: https://git.internal/redwood/payments/commit/ab12cd3

paul: ok I'll approve once you post the helm command + release-note blurb. also add a rollback playbook snippet.

alice: helm command (will run from CICD):
```
helm upgrade payments-service charts/payments \
  --namespace prod-eu-west-1 \
  --set image.tag=2026-03-20-ab12cd3 \
  --set feature.toggle.null-safe-charge=true \
  --timeout 10m
```

alice: release-note blurb: "payments-service: added null-safety guard for charge_ref during rollout to protect legacy workers; temporary guard will be removed after consumers are upgraded. No data migrations required."

paul: rollback playbook (short): 
- if error rate > 1% for 5m -> run `/deploy rollback payments-service eu-west-1`
- if partial failures isolated to workers -> disable feature flag and start patch release
- notify customers via status page + attach runbook

paul: approving now `/deploy approve payments-service eu-west-1 --reason "null-safe guard enabled"` :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: [automated] approval received by paul. proceeding with manual rollforward. canary will resume.

carol: monitoring dashboards set, alert thresholds lowered for first 30m. tagging the canary with `migration-safe=true` in release metadata. :eyes: 

ben: live metrics look good at 3m post-resume — errors back to baseline. shipping release notes now. :shipit:

alice: thanks team. will follow up with a short postmortem if anything pops.

paul: add a note to the release notes about the temporary guard and next steps to remove it in 2 weeks.

carol: noted. closing thread after 1h unless we see regressions.
